note: India's Census 2011 total and sex ratio 943: chapter teaches the final total as ~121.06 crore (MoSPI Table 1.1: 1210.57 million, M 623.12 / F 587.45) and SR 943 (NCERT Sociology + MoSPI). The bank item's exact count 1,210,854,977 comes from the Census state-level xlsx, which could not be fetched as text; the chapter additionally teaches NCERT's provisional exact total 1,210,193,422.

State population ranking Uttar Pradesh > Maharashtra > Bihar > West Bengal taught verbatim from NCERT legy201. The bank's exact state counts are from the Census xlsx (unfetchable as text), so the chapter teaches the ranking, not the exact counts.
Kerala sex ratio 1084 (highest among states) and West Bengal 950 taught from MoSPI Women & Men in India 2016, Tables 1.2/1.3; Puducherry 1037 also taught.

'Mouza' = revenue village is a land-records definition. None of the fetched allowed sources (PIB Census 2027 backgrounder, NCERT legy201/lesy102, MoSPI) defines 'mouza', so it is not taught in this chapter.

Most densely populated state: the paper's key is West Bengal because Bihar was not among its options. The chapter teaches the full NCERT ranking (Bihar 1102 highest, West Bengal 1029 second) and carries an exam_note explaining exactly this paper's situation.
Least population density: Arunachal Pradesh, 17 persons per sq km (NCERT legy201) — taught.

Highest urbanised state (Goa, 62.17% urban): the only fetched source carrying state-wise urbanisation shares was NIRDPR's Rural Development Statistics, hosted on an org.in domain, which fails this book's GOVT publisher pattern (only *.gov.in / *.nic.in). No NCERT/MoSPI quote for it was obtained, so the fact was dropped from the chapter and this PYQ is untaught.

Share of population below age 35 (65%): no fetched source gives this age-structure share. NCERT legy201 gives only the adolescent (10-19) share of 20.9%, which the chapter teaches; the below-35 figure is not taught.
Second most populated district (North 24 Parganas): district-level population rankings are not present in any fetched source; the chapter teaches state-level rankings only.

West Bengal literacy: the 2019 key (77.08%) used the provisional figure. The chapter teaches the final PCA figure 76.3% (MoSPI Table 3.3) and flags the provisional 77.08% in an exam_note, so students can answer either framing.
Union Territory with the highest sex ratio: Puducherry, 1037 (MoSPI Women & Men in India 2016 findings) — taught.

West Bengal district with the highest child sex ratio (Howrah): district-level child sex ratios are not present in any fetched source; the chapter teaches state-level CSR (India 918/919, West Bengal 956, Haryana 834, Arunachal 972) only.
2026-27 Census as India's first digital/paperless census: taught from the PIB Census 2027 backgrounder (first census by digital means, mobile-based collection, CMMS portal).
Sex ratio defined as the number of females per 1000 males: taught verbatim from NCERT lesy102 (Table 3 note).

Population of India 'at the time of the 2009 exam' (a few more than 1.10 billion) is a between-censuses current-affairs estimate, not a census statistic; the chapter teaches census totals (2001: ~102.86 crore provisional; 2011: ~121.06 crore) only.
